title: Build Array Where You Can Find The Maximum Exactly K Comparisons
summary: Given integers n, m, and k, construct an array arr with n elements, each between 1 and m, inclusive, such that the algorithm to find the maximum element requires exactly k comparisons.
statement: Given integers n, m, and k, construct an array arr with n elements, each between 1 and m, inclusive, such that the algorithm to find the maximum element requires exactly k comparisons. Calculate the number of such arrays modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count length-n arrays with values 1..m whose running maximum increases exactly k times.
hints: DP state needs processed length, current maximum, and record-increase count.
Append every value 1..m; only values above the current maximum increase cost.
Merge identical resulting states modulo the modulus.
Every array has a unique prior prefix and final value, so transitions count it exactly once.
editorial: Every array has a unique prior prefix and final value, so transitions count it exactly once.

tests.explanation: The six non-increasing-with-respect-to-the-first-maximum arrays have cost one.
Exactly five length-five binary arrays introduce a new maximum three times.
